result.summary:
STEP 0.5: docs/issues/ISS-0722.yaml (resolved) is the only prior issue on this code path but its root cause (manual mode silently dropped) is distinct and already fixed -- that fix (PR #1564) is what introduced this concatenation. A broader grep for related terms across docs/issues/*.yaml found no other genuine match (13 filename hits, 0 actually contain 'resolved_question'). VERDICT: distinct, new finding, not a recurrence.

STEP 1: Confirmed by direct reading (lib/letflow/exam/session.ex:707-882, lib/letflow/exam/question_set_resolver.ex:1-94, lib/letflow/design/iss0722-exam-manual-question-mode.md section 4.1). materialize_session/5 concatenates resolved_random ++ resolved_manual at session.ex:736-739 via Enum.with_index/1; both lists are shaped identically to QuestionSetResolver's @type resolved_question() (question_set_resolver.ex:46-51, no origin field). fetch_manual_questions/2 (session.ex:840-841) reuses the resolver's question_row() type by convention only. Design doc section 4.1 (lines 208-215) states manual-origin questions must NEVER be reordered by shuffle_questions?, currently enforced only by materialize_session/5's manual path never calling Enum.shuffle on resolved_manual -- a behavioral fact with no structural/type backing once concatenated.

What a fix touches: (1) materialize_session/5 concatenation at session.ex:736-739; (2) persist_session_questions/4 (session.ex:868-882), currently takes one flat list; (3) QuestionSetResolver's resolved_question() type/spec (question_set_resolver.ex:46-51,68) only if origin-tagging is chosen; (4) manual map construction at session.ex:724-734; (5) any existing test asserting on resolved's shape.

RECOMMENDATION: keep the two lists separate one call further into persist_session_questions/4, rather than tag-at-construction. Reasoning: tagging widens QuestionSetResolver's public type for a caller-side (session.ex) concern, blurring the module boundary the design doc explicitly protects (section 2, 'bypass don't generalize the resolver', line 361), and a tag alone doesn't structurally prevent a future Enum.shuffle(resolved) on the merged list -- it only makes the violation detectable after the fact, not a compile failure, which AC1 explicitly asks for. Separating the lists through persist_session_questions/4 (signature persist_session_questions(session_id, resolved_random, resolved_manual, actor_id, prefix)) makes the never-reorder invariant a structural fact of the call graph -- a future edit merging/reshuffling them would show up as a wrong-arity/wrong-variable compile error, not a silent semantic change. AC2 is also easier to keep provably true this way since resolved_random/resolved_manual's own construction logic (session.ex:715-734) doesn't change at all. CODE-DESIGNER still needs to specify sort_order computation for the separated-list design: preserve 'random block first, then manual block, sort_order continuous across both' (design doc section 4.2) -- e.g. Enum.with_index(resolved_random) then Enum.with_index(resolved_manual, length(resolved_random)).

Both AC1 and AC2's factual premises independently verified by direct reading, not trusted from issue prose.
result.next_action: Route to Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER fix design) -- recommend list-separation direction into persist_session_questions/4
